fluff.overview:
The Viking IIC is a 90-ton Clan-technology assault BattleMech introduced in 3095 as a comprehensive rebuild of the original Viking design. Born from Grumium Creations' desperate attempt to avoid closure, the project began as a simple refit of existing Vikings held in the Rasalhague Dominion's touman, upgrading them with advanced Clan weapons and equipment. When Grumium recognized the design's potential, the company licensed the Viking IIC to Arc-Royal MechWorks for full production.

Though Grumium's efforts to stave off bankruptcy ultimately failed, the design survived the company's demise. Arc-Royal MechWorks continued production, serving primarily the Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces, with limited numbers reaching the Republic of the Sphere and Clan Wolf-in-Exile. The Viking IIC builds upon its predecessor's fire support philosophy while incorporating the devastating capabilities of Clan missile technology and the extraordinary protection of hardened armor.
fluff.capabilities:
The Viking IIC retains the fire support philosophy of its predecessor while incorporating significant Clan-technology improvements. Four Clan LRM launchers, a pair of Type XX "Great Bow" LRM-20s and two Type XVI LRM-15s, deliver withering long-range fire without the minimum range limitations of their Inner Sphere counterparts, allowing the design to punish approaching enemies at any distance. All four launchers are linked to advanced Artemis V fire control systems for exceptional accuracy.

Defensive armament consists of two Mustang 4.5 ER Micro Lasers mounted in the side torsos and four Series IX machine guns in the legs for anti-infantry work. The defining feature of the Viking IIC is its massive thirty-one tons of GC Hardened Slab armor, providing extraordinary protection that makes the 'Mech extremely difficult to bring down. This protection comes at a significant cost, however, as the dense armor reduces the design's top speed to just 43 kilometers per hour, making it one of the slowest assault 'Mechs in active service.

CASE II systems in both side torsos protect against ammunition explosions while preserving the affected components. The design's limited ammunition reserves of roughly eight tons remain its primary operational constraint, requiring the Viking IIC to maintain proximity to supply lines or risk running dry at a critical moment.
fluff.history:
The Viking IIC emerged from the twilight of Grumium Creations, the same small manufacturer that had produced the original Viking for decades. By the early thirty-first century, the Grumium factory had transitioned through multiple political masters, from the Free Rasalhague Republic to Clan Ghost Bear to the Rasalhague Dominion. Facing closure, Grumium's engineers undertook an ambitious project to refit existing Viking airframes with Clan technology, incorporating advanced missile launchers, hardened armor, and improved fire control systems.

The initial prototypes proved promising enough that Grumium licensed the design to Arc-Royal MechWorks, ensuring the Viking IIC's survival even after the Grumium factory eventually closed. Arc-Royal MechWorks began full production, with the 'Mech entering service primarily with the Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces. Grumium itself managed to place the design into actual production around 3140 before finally ceasing operations.

The Viking IIC proved its combat worth during the Second Combine-Dominion War. On Thule, a Star of Viking IICs from the Fourteenth Provisional Garrison Cluster surprised warriors of the Thirteenth Sun Zhang Cadre who had dismissed the fire support 'Mechs as easy targets. The Dominion warriors closed distance and delivered accurate missile fire that devastated the Combine troops before reinforcements arrived to finish the engagement.

The LCAF also employed Viking IICs effectively during the defense of Tamarind in 3138, where the Fourth Royal Guards used them to supplement assault operations against the Unified Duchy Military Command. Under sustained fire from Viking IIC formations, opposing forces were repeatedly forced to retreat and regroup, demonstrating the design's value as a durable fire support anchor in defensive operations.
fluff.deployment: Before Grumium Creations shuttered its facilities, refitted Viking IICs proliferated throughout the Rasalhague Dominion's touman. Though Clan Wolf-in-Exile manufactures the design at its Arc-Royal facility, the 'Mech's low top speed does not suit the Clan's aggressive battle philosophy, resulting in limited adoption among Clan warriors. The Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces procures the majority of Arc-Royal MechWorks' production runs, valuing the design's heavy armor and long-range firepower for defensive operations. The Republic of the Sphere has also purchased limited numbers. The Viking IIC has seen combat during the Second Combine-Dominion War and in the defense of Tamarind in 3138 against the Unified Duchy Military Command, proving itself as a durable fire support platform in both engagements.
